back_en: Now we'll remind the brain and body what gratitude feels like.
Recall something small that happened recently that you're grateful for, like a friend's smile or sun on your skin.
Now close your eyes. Go back to that moment as if you're there again, and feel gratitude right now.
Now think of something you almost never notice, like your eyesight, or hot water coming from the tap.
Close your eyes. Slow down for a second and try to really feel gratitude for this.

flags.reason: "попробуй правда почувствовать" reads as translated "try to really feel"

back_en: Each time you do this exercise, try to find something new rather than repeat the same thing. That's what turns on the logical part of the brain.
Now think of who you're grateful to.
Close your eyes. Picture that person's face, hear their voice, and try to really feel gratitude in your chest as you breathe.
Now think about what we all take most for granted. Breathing. You're breathing. You're alive.
Close your eyes. Feel the breath moving inside, and be glad you're alive on this beautiful planet.
This exercise was to remind the body what gratitude feels like. Now try to feel that same gratitude, but without a logical reason.
If you want, put your hands on your heart.
If you don't feel anything, that's fine. You can't force it. It's a skill, and it grows every time.
Next time a dark thought creeps in, do this right on the spot.
Open your eyes when you're ready.
